script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

We open on a cozy, middle-class living room. The air is thick with the scent of freshly brewed coffee. Sunlight streams through a window, illuminating a family photo on the mantle.

NATALIE (40s, warm, caring) sits on the couch, scrolling through her phone. Her husband, JASON (40s, anxious, loving), enters, dressed in a suit. He holds a newspaper in one hand and a folder in the other.

JASON
(concerned)
Natalie, have you seen this? The company is downsizing. They're letting go of a quarter of the staff.

Natalie looks up, her expression turning to concern.

NATALIE
(surprised)
What? When did this happen?

JASON
(frustrated)
Just this morning. I got the call during my commute. They didn't even give us a warning. I'm lucky I made it to the office to pick up my things before they locked me out.

Natalie places a comforting hand on his shoulder.

NATALIE
(sympathetic)
Oh, Jason. I'm so sorry. This must be devastating for you. What are you going to do?

Jason sighs, staring at the floor.

JASON
(resolute)
I don't know. I'll start looking for something new, I suppose. I can't just sit around at home. I need to provide for our family.

NATALIE
(encouraging)
Of course. I'll help you in any way I can. We'll get through this together.

INT. KITCHEN - LATER

Natalie and Jason sit at the kitchen table, surrounded by resumés and job listings. Their teenage daughter, SAMANTHA (16, sarcastic, observant), enters.

SAMANTHA
(skeptical)
Mom, Dad, another job search? How many is this now?

Jason looks up, weary.

JASON
(defeated)
Several, Samantha. And this one might be the most difficult yet.

Samantha rolls her eyes.

SAMANTHA
(sarcastic)
Wow, great. Just what I wanted to hear when I got home from school.

Natalie puts a comforting hand on Samantha's shoulder.

NATALIE
(gentle)
Samantha, we're all in this together. Your father needs our support right now.

Samantha sighs, a small smile playing on her lips.

SAMANTHA
(reluctant)
Okay, I'll try to be more understanding. But I still don't see why you can't just find a different job in the same field.

Jason looks at his wife, a determined glint in his eye.

JASON
(decisive)
This time, I want to do something different. I don't want to keep working in a field that no longer values my contributions. I want to explore new opportunities and find a career that truly fulfills me.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jason sits at a table, laptop in front of him. Natalie enters, carrying a cup of coffee.

NATALIE
(encouraging)
You're making progress, Jason. I'm proud of you.

JASON
(grateful)
Thank you, Natalie. I couldn't do this without you.

They share a warm smile.

INT. LIBRARY - DAY

Jason and Natalie sit at a table, surrounded by piles of books. Samantha enters, carrying a stack of her own.

SAMANTHA
(skeptical)
Another day at the library? Really?

JASON
(determined)
Yes, Samantha. This time, I'm serious about finding a new career. I'm exploring every option, and the library is a great resource for that.

Samantha rolls her eyes but sits down to join them. Together, they dive back into their research.

INT. FAMILY ROOM - NIGHT

The family gathers around the TV, watching the evening news. The report focuses on a local entrepreneur, LUCY (30s, charismatic, ambitious), who has built a successful business from the ground up.

NATALIE
(excited)
Jason, look at this! This woman started her business with nothing, and now she's a success story. Maybe you could do something like that.

JASON
(intrigued)
I hadn't considered starting my own business, but now that you mention it...

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

Jason and Natalie sit at the table, brainstorming business ideas. Samantha enters, carrying a stack of papers.

SAMANTHA
(skeptical)
Mom, Dad, another business idea? Are you sure you're not just trying to distract yourselves from the job search?

NATALIE
(encouraging)
Samantha, this isn't a distraction. We're exploring all of our options. And Jason's idea for a green energy consulting firm could be truly groundbreaking.

Jason looks at his wife and daughter, a glint of determination in his eye.

JASON
(resolved)
I'm going to do it, Samantha. I'm going to start my own business.

Samantha smiles, genuinely proud of her father.

SAMANTHA
(supportive)
I'll help you any way I can, Dad. I believe in you.

INT. HOME OFFICE - DAY

Jason sits at his makeshift home office, working on the business plan for his green energy consulting firm. Natalie enters, holding a stack of papers.

NATALIE
(proud)
I've got some good news, Jason. I've been working on the financial projections for your business, and the numbers look promising.

Jason looks up, a wide smile spreading across his face.

JASON
(grateful)
Thank you, Natalie. I couldn't have done this without you.

They share a loving embrace.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

Jason presents his business plan to a group of potential investors at the community center. He speaks passionately about his vision for the future of green energy and the positive impact his consulting firm will have on the environment and the community.

The investors listen intently, impressed by his conviction and knowledge.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

The family sits in the living room, watching the local news. The anchor reports on Jason's successful pitch to the investors and his new green energy consulting firm.

NATALIE
(proud)
Jason, this is incredible! Your hard work and determination have paid off.

JASON
(grateful)
I couldn't have done it without your support, Natalie, and Samantha's help, too.

They all share a proud moment, knowing that their family has overcome a difficult transition and come out stronger on the other side.

FADE OUT.
